item.text: I’m tightening this to baseline-adjusted life chances: macro gains, household access, job quality, and whether gains reached marginalized groups. I’ll use a small set of source searches, then synthesize only the strongest claim-level evidence.

item.text:
**Assessment:** Mixed, leaning positive. In 2024 Jokowi left Indonesians with better average life chances than he inherited in the narrow sense of macro stability, poverty reduction, and health-service access, but the gains were incomplete, uneven, and constrained by weak job quality, learning deficits, and persistent exclusion in remote and marginalized regions.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024 Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280) - World Bank, 2024-10-02. Indonesia was growing at about 5%, poverty fell from 17.5% in 2023 to 15.8% in 2024, and the external position stayed manageable. Best direct evidence that ordinary people’s baseline materially improved in 2024 despite a difficult global environment. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.5`, `6B.6`.

- [IMF Staff Completes 2024 Article IV Mission to Indonesia](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/14/pr24221-imf-staff-completes-2024-article-iv-mission-to-indonesia) - IMF, 2024-06-14. IMF said growth stayed strong, inflation was contained, and fiscal/monetary frameworks were prudent and shock-ready. This supports the case that Jokowi left a more stable platform for future opportunity, though not a complete transformation of life chances. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.5`, `6B.6`.

- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) - World Health Organization, 2024. WHO credits Indonesia with 90% health coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, and better access to essential services regardless of gender, age, or disability. This is strong evidence that basic life chances improved through broader and more inclusive service access. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.4`, `6B.7`.

- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) - World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. Mobile JKN simplified enrollment and payments, helped informal contributors, and lowered BPJS administrative costs, though digital access gaps limited impact. This is durable, institutional improvement rather than one-off relief. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.9`, `6B.4`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`.

- [Bappenas perkuat dukungan untuk anak-anak dan keluarga rentan](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/press-releases/bappenas-perkuat-dukungan-untuk-anak-anak-dan-keluarga-rentan) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-04-25. Regsosek was presented as a way to improve targeting, delivery, accountability, and transparency of social assistance for poor and vulnerable households. This supports better life chances by making public support more precise and less arbitrary. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.9`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`.

- [Blueprint get children back to school in Indonesia](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/stories/blueprint-get-children-back-school-indonesia) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-08-23. The back-to-school campaign returned nearly 37,000 children to learning and helped prevent about 149,000 dropouts since 2021. This is direct evidence of improved opportunity, especially for children at risk of being left behind. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.9`.

- [Indonesia - Learning Poverty Brief 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082924151529593) - World Bank / UNESCO, 2024-04-01. The brief says learning poverty still threatened human capital and poverty reduction, showing that schooling quality and opportunity remained deeply unequal. This is the clearest counterweight to the positive macro story. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.9`.

- [Indonesia's dwindling middle class seen dimming economic outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-dwindling-middle-class-seen-dimming-economic-outlook-3610865) - Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-09-11. Reuters reported layoffs and weaker job opportunities squeezing working- and middle-class Indonesians, with some households unable to afford basics. This is strong negative evidence that macro gains did not fully translate into broad, durable life chances. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.6`, `6B.8`.

- [Social Protection Inclusion in Indonesia’s Remote Areas](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099062624071020814) - World Bank, 2024-06-01. Poor and vulnerable households in remote areas still faced barriers to accessing social protection, so improved design did not become equal real-world reach. This undercuts any claim that better national averages meant universally better life chances. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.9`, `6B.8`, `6B.7`.

- [Indonesia racism, discrimination against Indigenous Papuans](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18. HRW documented discrimination, denial of health and education, and security-force abuses against Indigenous Papuans. That is strong evidence that ordinary people in a major marginalized region did not inherit materially better life chances in any even-handed sense. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.6`, `6B.7`.

- [Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia's democracy icon, leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Reuters’ end-of-term framing emphasizes strong growth and infrastructure but also patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity. This matters because life chances were improved under a politically fragile and uneven governance model, not a cleanly inclusive one. QIDs: `6B.10`; also `6B.8`, `6B.9`, `4B.2`.

**Search Gap**
- The strongest positive evidence is macro and sectoral, especially health and social protection.
- I did not find a single 2024 source showing broad, across-the-board improvement in job quality, school learning, housing access, and marginalized-region equality all at once.
- So the best reading is: ordinary Indonesians generally ended 2024 better off than they began, but not equally better off, and not with fully secured upward mobility.
